name: BACH_0084
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (>99%)** · Confident · Read in turn
Single-class conformal set, second model and all 5 neighbors agree [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive >99%, InSitu <1% | Near-certain |
| Conformal set | {Invasive} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.996 / 64th percentile | Typical, sound input |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes | Same top class |
| Similar cases | 5/5 Invasive | Unanimous neighbors |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 6, 8, 11) · ↑ invasive · Strongest concept association with invasive carcinoma · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (regions 6, 8, 9) · ↑ invasive · Second-strongest invasive association · Validated
- **Variation in nuclear size** (regions 4, 5, 6) · context · 90th percentile; mean nuclear size only 10th · Measured
- **Gland / tubule formation** (region 10) · ↓ invasive · Strongest in region 10, the lowest-risk region · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Removal effect is 0.002 versus random (CI −0.005 to 0.007), so not shown to reflect the classifier. Unreliable here: necrosis (3/20), normal lobules (0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Cell measurements cover only regions 4–6; the other regions are unmeasured.
- Region 10 scores lower (49% risk); a focal or mixed lesion may be under-called.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 6, 8, 11**: Confirm tumor infiltrating the stroma.
2. **Regions 4, 5, 6**: Confirm small nuclei with variable size.
3. **Region 10**: Look for glands or benign lobules in this lowest-risk region.
